why: M5a's FIRST step is to measure a representative upper envelope, because the only datum behind
revision 23's proposed 120 was a single 7-second one-file run — which says nothing about a cold
linter-cache bootstrap or a large staged changeset. This hook BLOCKS, so a false timeout changes
The constant is the measured envelope PLUS EXPLICIT HEADROOM: the envelope is measured on one
developer Mac while the constant is asserted in CI across a Linux leg and different Darwin
hardware, so a value fitted tightly to this measurement would make cell 13's clean slow-path case
fail against a CORRECT implementation on a slower runner or a slower network.

measuredOn.note: fast Apple Silicon laptop on a fast network — the OPTIMISTIC end of the range

measurements.note: downloads every enabled linter; produced a 1.4 GB cache. This is the envelope driver.

constantRationale: The normal path is 2-7 seconds warm; the cold bootstrap is a once-per-machine 30.8 seconds here.
180 gives ~6x headroom over the measured cold envelope, which covers a slower network, a slower
runner and a colder cache without the ceiling ever being reached on a healthy run. The timeout
exists to bound a HANG, not to police the normal path.
Revision 23's 120 was not wrong as a number — it was unjustified. This records the justification.
limits: The cold measurement used an isolated TRUNK_CACHE rather than wiping the developer's real cache,
so it is a true cold bootstrap but on this machine's network only.
No Linux measurement was taken: the pre-commit hook does not run in CI, so the Linux leg only
asserts the CONSTANT, never the envelope.
